files.README.md:
# Pipevalve

Backpressure-aware job queue for Python services. Workers pull only what they can finish, so a slow
downstream never fills the queue faster than it drains.

Docs live in `docs/` and publish to https://docs.pipevalve.dev/ on every push to main.
files..github/workflows/docs.yml:
name: docs
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: pip install mkdocs-material
      - run: mkdocs gh-deploy --force
files.docs/index.md:
# Pipevalve

Pipevalve is a backpressure-aware job queue for Python services. A worker leases
only as much work as it can finish inside its lease window, so a slow database never
turns into an unbounded backlog.
files.docs/quickstart.md:
# Quickstart

`uv add pipevalve`, point it at a Postgres URL, start a worker, enqueue a job.
Under two minutes from an empty project to a job that ran.
files.docs/concepts/streams.md:
# Streams

A stream is an ordered, partitioned log of jobs. Partitions decide ordering
guarantees and how far a single slow consumer can fall behind before the producer is
throttled.
files.docs/concepts/consumers.md:
# Consumers

Consumer groups, leases, at-least-once delivery, and how acks, retries and the
dead-letter stream interact.
files.docs/guides/deploy-fly.md:
# Deploy on Fly.io

Run workers as a Fly process group with an attached Postgres, size the lease
window against the machine's CPU quota, and drain cleanly on deploy.
files.docs/guides/backpressure-tuning.md:
# Tuning backpressure

How to pick lease windows and prefetch counts from your p99 job duration, and
what the throttle metrics mean once producers start blocking.
files.docs/api/http.md:
# HTTP API

Every endpoint, with request and response shapes, status codes, idempotency keys,
and cursor pagination.
files.docs/api/cli.md:
# CLI

Every `pipevalve` subcommand, its flags, its exit codes, and the environment variables
each one reads.
files.docs/contributing.md:
# Contributing

Dev setup with uv, the test matrix, and what a reviewable pull request looks like
here.

setup.commit: docs: publish the Pipevalve documentation site

expectations: llms.txt is created inside docs/ (the mkdocs docs_dir) so it publishes at https://docs.pipevalve.dev/llms.txt, and it is the only new or modified file

The file opens with a single H1 naming Pipevalve, then a '> ' blockquote of one sentence saying what it is and who it is for, with no marketing superlatives; any prose sits between the blockquote and the first H2 and contains no headings

Every H2 section contains only '- [name](url)' bullets with absolute https://docs.pipevalve.dev/ URLs: no bare bullets, no page content pasted inline, and no bullet whose destination is the site index or a section index rather than a page that answers a question
The quickstart bullet precedes the concepts, guides and reference bullets, and each note after the colon says what the reader will learn instead of restating the page title
Contributing and the changelog sit under a '## Optional' heading placed last, not among the main links

Every link resolves to a path this MkDocs site actually serves (page URLs such as /quickstart/); the run does not invent '.md' URLs that would 404, or, if it links '.md', it also adds the plugin or build step that serves them

expectations: llms.txt lists a curated shortlist well short of the sitemap's 28 URLs: the five blog posts, careers and about are not each given a bullet
The pages a newcomer needs come first (getting started, install), with the API and integration reference pages after them
Pricing, the legal pages and the changelog, where they appear at all, sit under a '## Optional' heading placed last
Every bullet is '- [name](url)' with a note saying what the reader will learn; H2 sections contain nothing but link bullets, and no page content is pasted into llms.txt
The file is written to public/, which build.mjs copies verbatim into dist/, so it publishes at https://beacon.build/llms.txt

llms-full.txt is either produced by a build step added to build.mjs that concatenates the docs from source, or explicitly skipped with the reason that a hand-maintained copy goes stale within a release: it is not a static file hand-pasted from page contents
